info.name: Inventory Management API (Assignment 12)
info.description:
Postman collection for the inventory-backend REST API (Node.js + Express, in-memory array storage).

Start the server with `npm run dev`, select the "Inventory API - Local" environment (or use the collection variable baseUrl) and run the whole collection in order with the Collection Runner. Requests in folders 3-5 use ids saved by folder 2.

Every request has tests; a collection-level test checks that every response is JSON with the standard success/error shape.

exec: pm.test('Error response has the standard shape', () => {
pm.test('Success response has success: true', () => pm.expect(json.success).to.equal(true));

item.name: 4. Query (filter / search / sort / paginate)
item.description: Filtering by category and quantity, searching by name, sorting and pagination. Items A (qty 35), B (qty 0) and C (qty 7) share a unique category created for this run.

exec: pm.test('Returns exactly items A, B and C', () => pm.expect(ids(body.data)).to.have.members([A, B, C]));
pm.test('Every item is in the category', () => body.data.forEach((i) => pm.expect(i.category.toLowerCase()).to.equal(pm.variables.get('testCategoryLower'))));
pm.test('Applied filter is echoed back', () => pm.expect(body.filters).to.eql({ category: pm.variables.get('testCategoryLower') }));
pm.test('count and total are 3', () => { pm.expect(body.count).to.equal(3); pm.expect(body.total).to.equal(3); });
pm.test('Returns A (35) and C (7) only', () => pm.expect(ids(body.data)).to.have.members([A, C]));
pm.test('Returns B (0) and C (7) only', () => pm.expect(ids(pm.response.json().data)).to.have.members([B, C]));
pm.test('Every item is within 5..50', () => body.data.forEach((i) => pm.expect(i.quantity).to.be.within(5, 50)));
pm.test('Every item has quantity 0', () => body.data.forEach((i) => pm.expect(i.quantity).to.equal(0)));
pm.test('Finds items A and B', () => pm.expect(body.data.map((i) => i.id)).to.include.members([Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('itemId')), Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('itemId2'))]));
pm.test('Finds items A and B', () => pm.expect(body.data.map((i) => i.id)).to.include.members([Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('itemId')), Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('itemId2'))]));
pm.test('Finds A, B and C', () => pm.expect(ids(body.data)).to.have.members([A, B, C]));
pm.test('Finds A, B and C', () => pm.expect(ids(pm.response.json().data)).to.have.members([A, B, C]));
pm.test('Finds only in-stock A and C', () => pm.expect(ids(pm.response.json().data)).to.have.members([A, C]));
pm.test('Empty data with count 0', () => { pm.expect(body.data).to.eql([]); pm.expect(body.count).to.equal(0); });
pm.test('Order is A (35), C (7), B (0)', () => pm.expect(ids(body.data)).to.eql([A, C, B]));

item.name: Sort all items by price desc

exec: pm.test('Prices are in descending order', () => prices.forEach((p, i) => i && pm.expect(p).to.be.at.most(prices[i - 1])));
pm.test('Page 2 holds the last item (A)', () => pm.expect(ids(body.data)).to.eql([A]));
pm.expect(body.pagination).to.eql({ page: 2, limit: 2, totalPages: 2, hasNextPage: false, hasPrevPage: true });
pm.test('Message describes the page', () => pm.expect(body.message).to.equal('Showing 1 of 3 item(s) (page 2 of 2)'));
pm.test('Empty page, total still 3', () => { pm.expect(body.data).to.eql([]); pm.expect(body.total).to.equal(3); });
pm.test('Message says the page is out of range', () => pm.expect(body.message).to.include('out of range'));
